description: v3 multi-step bench inspired by aider/SWE-bench. 6 multi-step tasks: 4 graph-heavy (where wrong starting point cascades) + 2 adversarial literal (rg should win). Each task has objectively verifiable ground truth. Scoring: must_contain set (all required tokens present, case-insensitive). Run N=2 per (task, mode) for variance. Track trajectory: tool_uses, distinct_tools, distinct_files_read.

puzzles.question: Two-step task. (1) Among Rust functions defined in src-tauri/src/service/ (any depth), identify the TOP 2 functions by NUMBER OF DISTINCT incoming callers (other Rust files that call them via `invoke` edges). (2) For each of those 2 functions, name ONE other Rust file in the codeterm repo that calls it. Output as a 2-row list: 'function_name @ defining_file — caller: caller_file'. The top function should have ≥3 more callers than the runner-up.

Two-step task. (1) Across ALL Tauri commands defined in this repo, group them by their first underscore-separated segment (e.g. 'mux_create_workspace' → 'mux'; 'mesh_get_status' → 'mesh'). (2) Report which prefix has the MOST distinct commands and the count for that prefix. Final answer must include the prefix string and the integer count.

Among files inside src-tauri/src/service/ (only one level deep, not subdirectories), find the SINGLE file that has the most other Rust files referencing it (incoming dependents). Output the file path. (Hint: this file is a module-root.)

Among ALL Tauri commands in this repo, find the top 5 ranked by NUMBER of distinct invocation sites in TypeScript code (i.e. count how many times `invoke('command_name')` or equivalent appears across .ts/.tsx files, grouped by command name). List the 5 command names in any order. The top one should appear by a wide margin (~3× the next).
Where in the Rust source code is the literal string 'protected workspace has no project map' written? Provide the file path and line number.
How many DISTINCT files inside src-tauri/src/api/ (any depth — search recursively into all subdirectories) contain at least one call to `.unwrap_or_else(`? Just answer with the integer.

scoring.correctness: 1.0 if all must_contain tokens present (case-insensitive substring); 0.5 if at least half; 0.0 otherwise.
trajectory_metrics: distinct_tools (worker lists which tool TYPES used: rg|Read|Bash|codeterm-map|other)
distinct_files_read (count of unique file paths Read)
